title: Composition for the dualizing complex
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
and the coefficient
conventions, $A=A_{E,n}$, put $s=\Spec k$, and let
$d:F\to X$ be a
separated finite-type
morphism with $a_X$ and $a_F=a_X\circ d$
exceptionally admissible. Then there is a
canonical isomorphism

$$
Rd^!\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\omega_{F,A},
$$

functorial in $d$, where $\omega_{X,A}$, $\omega_{F,A}$ are the
dualizing complexes of
[def-trf-dualizing-complex] and $Rd^!$ is the
exceptional inverse image of
$d$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal D_T=D^b_{ctf}(T,A)$, $L_f=Rf_!$ and $R_f=Rf^!$. By [def-trf-admissibility], the three morphisms $d,a_X,a_F$ have specified adjunctions $L_f\dashv R_f$ on these categories. The hypotheses give admissibility for the two structure morphisms; for $d$ the same definition explicitly states that every separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes is admissible. Thus all three adjunctions have the same finite coefficient ring $A$ and the same constructible finite-Tor domains. Clause (3) of [prop-functor-package] supplies the natural isomorphism $\alpha:L_{a_X}L_d\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{a_F}$, with its identity and associativity equations. Only this compact-support composition clause is used from that package.

Apply [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] to $L_d$ and $L_{a_X}$: $R_dR_{a_X}$ is right adjoint to $L_{a_X}L_d$, with pasted counit. The same left functor has right adjoint $R_{a_F}$: explicitly transport $L_{a_F}\dashv R_{a_F}$ along $\alpha$ by the natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(L_{a_X}L_dK,N)\xrightarrow{h\mapsto h\alpha_K^{-1}}\operatorname{Hom}(L_{a_F}K,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K,R_{a_F}N)$. The canonical right-adjoint comparison in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] therefore gives a natural isomorphism $\chi_{d,a_X}:R_dR_{a_X}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{a_F}$. More explicitly, $\chi_{d,a_X,N}$ is the $L_{a_F}\dashv R_{a_F}$ transpose of
$$L_{a_F}R_dR_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}}L_{a_X}L_dR_dR_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{L_{a_X}\varepsilon_d}L_{a_X}R_{a_X}N\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_{a_X}}N.$$
This specifies the comparison rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between the objects; the inverse is the reverse right-adjoint comparison. The displayed formula uses precisely the pasted counit asserted by the cited node.

The constant complex $A_s$ is in $\mathcal D_s$: its sole cohomology sheaf is the constant finite rank-one free $A$-module, hence constructible. For every sheaf $M$ of $A$-modules in degree zero, the free rank-one complex $A_s$ itself is a flat model and $A_s\otimes_A^L M=M$, so cohomology outside degree zero vanishes. This gives Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with the finite coefficient ring of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Evaluate $\chi_{d,a_X}$ at $A_s$. By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], $R_{a_X}A_s=\omega_{X,A}$ and $R_{a_F}A_s=\omega_{F,A}$. The resulting component is the required canonical isomorphism $R_d\omega_{X,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{F,A}$.

source.place: Second paragraph: evaluate the composition isomorphism at the constant complex

proof.text:
For further composition take $e:H\to F$, with $a_H=a_F e$, and use the same notation for all separated finite-type composites. Write $\alpha_{g,f}:L_gL_f\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{gf}$ for compact-support composition. As in Step 2, [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] gives $\theta_{e,d}:R_eR_d\xrightarrow{\sim}R_{de}$, whose component at $M$ is the $L_{de}\dashv R_{de}$ transpose of
$$\varepsilon_{d,M}\circ L_d(\varepsilon_{e,R_dM})\circ\alpha_{d,e,R_eR_dM}^{-1}.$$
Thus $\theta_{e,d}$ is exactly the conjugate of $\alpha_{d,e}^{-1}$ under the composite adjunction, in the terminology of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. The same applies to every $\chi$ in Step 2.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], clause (2), to each compact-support comparison and an identity square on the remaining factor; its composite adjunctions have exactly the pasted counits used in Step 4. Clause (3) changes the intermediate composite adjunction to the specified adjunction for the composite morphism. Together with composition of conjugates in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], this identifies
$$\chi_{e,a_F}\circ R_e\chi_{d,a_X},\qquad
\chi_{de,a_X}\circ(\theta_{e,d}R_{a_X})$$
as the conjugates, respectively, of the two left-functor transformations
$$ (\alpha_{a_X,d}^{-1}L_e)\circ\alpha_{a_F,e}^{-1},\qquad
(L_{a_X}\alpha_{d,e}^{-1})\circ\alpha_{a_X,de}^{-1}.$$
Both have source $L_{a_H}$ and target $L_{a_X}L_dL_e$; the right adjoints have source $R_eR_dR_{a_X}$ and target $R_{a_H}$. The associativity equation from [prop-functor-package],
$$\alpha_{a_F,e}\circ(\alpha_{a_X,d}L_e)=\alpha_{a_X,de}\circ(L_{a_X}\alpha_{d,e}),$$
makes these inverse composites equal. Their conjugates are consequently equal. This proves the further-composition equation as equality of natural transformations, before evaluation at $A_s$.

proof.text:
For identities, let $\lambda_T:L_{\mathrm{id}_T}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D_T}$ be the compact-support unit isomorphism of [prop-functor-package]. Conjugate $\lambda_T^{-1}:\mathrm{id}\to L_{\mathrm{id}_T}$ between $L_{\mathrm{id}_T}\dashv R_{\mathrm{id}_T}$ and $\mathrm{id}\dashv\mathrm{id}$, using [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Its component formula is the canonical isomorphism
$$u_{T,M}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,M}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}^{-1}:R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M\xrightarrow{\sim}M.$$
Indeed the second adjunction has identity unit, so the displayed formula is direct substitution in the conjugate formula. In particular $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,M}=u_{T,M}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}M}$.

proof.text:
For the source identity and $g:T\to U$, substitute the unit equation $\alpha_{g,\mathrm{id}_T}=L_g\lambda_T$ from [prop-functor-package] into the defining transpose of Step 2. It becomes
$$\varepsilon_{g,M}\circ L_g(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{id}_T,R_gM}\circ\lambda_{T,R_{\mathrm{id}_T}R_gM}^{-1})
=\varepsilon_{g,M}\circ L_g(u_{T,R_gM}).$$
The right side is the transpose of $u_{T,R_gM}$ under $L_g\dashv R_g$. Injectivity of this adjunction bijection gives $\chi_{\mathrm{id}_T,g,M}=u_{T,R_gM}$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-98863bc6a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full. It is one commit changing only the item and its report, with no new nodes, no unit changes, and nothing in fixes/. The statement matches the blueprint text in both the master and main-20261015 snapshots (only the order number differs). The coefficient category is D^b_ctf(-,A_{E,n}) on the small pro-etale site throughout, the same as in def-trf-admissibility, def-trf-dualizing-complex and def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude. Step 1: admissibility gives the specified adjunction for every separated finite-type map, so it covers d, and prop-functor-package clause (3) gives compact-support composition with its identity and associativity laws. Step 2: I recomputed chi from rightAdjointUniq_hom_counit (Unique.lean:133) and naturality of alpha; it is the stated transpose of eps_aX∘L_aX eps_d∘alpha^{-1}, in the stated direction. Step 3 is elementary: A_s is constant free rank one with Tor amplitude [0,0] taken directly from the definition, not inferred from constructibility. Step 4: theta_{e,d} and chi are the conjugates of alpha^{-1} under def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate (conjugateEquiv, Mates.lean:275); I checked the component formula. Step 5: I instantiated lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting clause (2) (mateEquiv_hcomp, Mates.lean:209) with an identity square to get R_e chi_{d,aX} and theta_{e,d}R_aX. The two composite adjunctions on L_aX L_d L_e have the same counit, a one-line identity the step leaves implicit, which I accept. With conjugateEquiv_comp (Mates.lean:350) and the associativity equation, which type-checks, the composition law follows. Steps 6-8: I checked u = eps_id∘lambda^{-1}, chi_{id,g} = u_{R_g} and chi_{f,id} = R_f(u), which hold even when the identity counit is not the identity (tested with unit and counit -id over F_3). Edge cases d = id, empty F, and n=1 versus n>1 all hold. proof_deps equals the union of the step uses, and the dependency closure does not reach the item, so there is no cycle. My rg search found no duplicate; lem-coef-finite-dualizing is a coefficient-change statement, not the same theorem. No SGA source is cited. I accept the declared tool use of prop-functor-package clause (3), which the blueprint proof itself invokes.
